relationship: Wisdom parallel: guarded silence in the presence of evil
rationale: Amos says the understanding person will be silent because the time is evil, following the description of hostility to reproof and corrupt judgment. The psalmist guards his mouth when the sinner stands against him, becoming mute and silent even from good things. Both connect restrained speech to a hostile moral setting. The psalm gives a personal concern about sinning with the tongue and continuing pain, rather than a rule that all speech in every evil time is forbidden.

relationship: Personification: building elements give voice amid judgment
rationale: Amos makes the temple's coffered ceilings wail in a scene of many fallen and imposed silence. Habakkuk says a stone cries from a wall, while condemning a house's shame and a city built through bloodshed. Both give voice to part of a building within an oracle against destructive wrongdoing. The temple ceilings are not identified with Habakkuk's wall, and the target's beetle from wood is preserved rather than rewritten as a speaking timber beam.
